context.description: The system prompt and tools the agent receives when starting a turn from scratch, without a session
context.cliInfo:
{{note}}

Expected baseline is the LOWER BOUND for one turn (CLI baseline + eager tool schemas only). The real input can exceed it with accumulated context and activated deferred tools; an exact value is measured after the first turn.
context.samplePlaceholder: Write a sample message → simulate cross-session context for that message
context.claudeDynamic: claude-cli: dynamic context is injected into the last user message instead of being sent as a separate system block (so it does not break the warm cache prefix).
context.noDynamic: There is no dynamic context for this message. The summary, session artifacts, and todo list are added during a turn in a real session and are not simulated here.
context.lazyDescription: The schema is not included in the turn. Only the name and summary stay in the Available Tools (load on demand) section of the system prompt. The agent activates the tools it needs for the next step with activate_tools.

settings.changeParentConfirm:
Should {{agent}} now inherit from {{parent}}?

Current values are preserved: every field is marked as an override, and you can release individual fields to the parent with Inherit.
settings.detachParentConfirm:
Should {{agent}} stop inheriting?

The current effective values will be frozen as its own values and future parent changes will no longer apply.
settings.builtinNote: This is a built-in system agent. The application resolves the {{role}} role from this definition. You can edit it directly without creating a copy. Changed fields apply to every workspace and are preserved across launches; untouched fields keep following the built-in definition and receive application updates. Reset all returns to the built-in definition. It cannot be deleted or disabled.
settings.inheritNote: This agent inherits from {{parent}}. Inherited fields follow parent changes, while overridden fields belong to this agent. Editing a field overrides it; use Inherit to release it.
settings.roleNote: This agent is the workspace customization of the built-in {{parent}} definition. While enabled, the application resolves the {{role}} role from it; disabling it returns to the built-in definition. Fields without overrides follow the built-in value.
settings.libraryParent: This profile inherits from an agent in the library. Manage its parent in Agent library.
settings.parentHelp: Choosing a parent preserves the current values as overrides. Removing inheritance freezes the effective values as this agent's own values. Changes are saved immediately.
settings.hooksWarning: ⚠️ PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks do not run under codex-cli, either for Codex's own shell/apply_patch tools or for TionHarness tools called through the MCP bridge. Therefore PostToolUse token optimization such as sqz is also disabled for this agent. Codex runs its tool loop in a separate child process and does not support forwarding hooks.
settings.thinkingHelp: Extended reasoning applies to tool-free chat with the anthropic provider. Under claude-cli, the selected level is passed to the subprocess and mapped to CLI effortLevel. High+ and Max deep-work tiers reach the CLI. Max is applied with CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=max because settings.json rejects it. Thinking disables parallel tool batches (think XOR batch). Off disables thinking entirely with MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0.
settings.thinkingOffHelp: Off + claude-cli: Claude Code 2.1.203 and newer do not make parallel tool calls while thinking is enabled. This setting restores parallel batches, making runs faster and cheaper at the cost of deep reasoning.
settings.permissionHelp: Read-only permits only reading tools. Ask shows an approval dialog for write and command tools; autonomous runs reject these actions when nobody can approve. For claude-cli, these modes map to plan, acceptEdits, and bypass.
settings.nativeWebSearchHelp: Allow the CLI provider to use its own web search. This is enabled by default and provider searches still appear in the activity trace. Turning it off disables Codex web_search and Claude CLI WebSearch/WebFetch; searches then use the bridged TionHarness tools so tracking and usage counts apply.
settings.nativeShellHelp: Off by default: Claude Code and Codex use the TionHarness shell when the shell bridge is enabled. Turn this on to also allow the provider's own shell. Native commands use the provider's permissions and run outside TionHarness shell approval and background process management.
settings.coordinatorHelp: Start new sessions opened by this agent in coordinator mode. The coordinator handbook and worker-management tools are available automatically. Existing sessions are unaffected, and the agent can return its own session to single-task mode with set_coordinator_mode.
settings.coordinatorPromptHelp: Added to the system context immediately after the shared coordinator handbook only while the session is in coordinator mode. Put agent-specific delegation instructions here instead of in the soul; it costs zero tokens while coordinator mode is off.
settings.toolsHelp: This agent can access every workspace-active tool by default. Change visibility or block only the tools you want to treat differently here. Only active workspace tools are listed. Changes are saved immediately{{inheritance}}.
